summary: Round 4 of M4.19, verified by mutation against the staged bytes. Invariants.java was restored byte-for-byte after every run (diff -q against an as-found copy), the throwaway probe class was deleted, the four untracked M4.16/M4.20 files are all still in place, and the staged hash still computes to d7c68450e6c1 with an empty unstaged diff. R3-1 IS CLOSED, and closed by measurement rather than by prose: (a) deleting the four-line no-CONTINUE arm at Invariants.java:188-191 now fails exactly one test, InvariantsAcrossChainsTest#aChainCarryingDELTASWithNoCONTINUEAtAllIsReportedAsABrokenLINK ('Expecting ArrayList: [] to contain: ["link"]'); (b) reducing firstAncestorWithDeltas to `return 0;` now fails exactly one test, InvariantsAcrossChainsTest#aLATERChainDISOWNINGAPredecessorThatCarriesDELTASIsReportedAsABrokenLINK. Each mutation was applied ALONE, so the two arms are pinned separately. The row at backlog.md:266 now names the arms instead of counting them and says why. R3-2 IS CLOSED and its corrected evidence reproduces: probed against the staged bytes, epoch 1 (Continue+delta, NO seal) / epoch 2 present-but-never-opened (Seal(0,3) alone) / epoch 3 (Continue(0,2,0)+delta resuming at 3) returns `[]`, while the same shape with epoch 2 ABSENT returns `[link: epoch 3 continues from epoch 2, which is NOT SEALED]` -- exactly the distinction the corrected M4.23 clause now draws, including the stated reason (the withdrawn early return). THE SPLIT PRESERVED EVERY KILL I had previously confirmed, re-measured one mutation at a time across both classes: the fold's `break` (kills aSECONDSeal..., offsetsBEYOND..., theFOLDStops...), checkLink's first-seal `break` (aSECONDSeal..., theFOLDStops...), the `upTo` first-seal `break` (same two), the `continuedAt` arm (TWOChainsCONTINUING...), the never-opened while-loop (offsetsAreINHERITED...), gutting neverOpened to `false` (same), `< from` -> `< from - 1` (InvariantsTest#anOverlapOfEXACTLYONERecordIsStillReportedAsI2), the `gap` else-if (aDeltaResumingABOVE... and aSECONDSeal...), the I1 arm, the `chain` arm, the I5 arm, the `prevSeq` arm, the NOT-SEALED arm, `lastOffset() + 1` -> `lastOffset()`, and the `prevEpoch() < 1` guard. Every one of the 17 tests across the two classes kills at least one mutation, so neither half of the split is vacuous and neither is carried by the other. THE SEAM IS HONEST: all 7 tests in InvariantsTest build exactly one chain and assert a within-chain predicate; all 10 in InvariantsAcrossChainsTest concern the link or the inheritance. The one that could be argued -- aChainCarryingDELTASWithNoCONTINUEAtAll, which builds a single chain -- is correctly on the across side: it asserts the ABSENCE of a join and is produced by inheritedOffsets. INVARIANTFIXTURES NEEDS NO TEST OF ITS OWN and adding one would be the wrong move: `put` and `delta` are each used by fixtures that assert isEmpty() AND by fixtures that assert a specific violation with specific offsets, so any drift in either breaks one side or the other -- measured indirectly, since mutations to the checker land on both classes through these helpers. FIXED_CLOCK is the one member nothing constrains, but the only mutation available to it (back to systemUTC) is the reverse of the fix, and the javadoc states the reason correctly. COST: the whole diff is under sequencer/src/test plus one backlog row, so no billed object-store request rate moves; readChain is one LIST plus one GET per chain ENTRY (a delta per segment) and the ancestry walk is per EPOCH, both on the allowed side of cost.md rules R1/R5/R6, and the O(E-squared) harness cost is already tracked as M4.24. TWO SMALLER OBSERVATIONS, deliberately not raised as findings because neither has a failure scenario a gate does not already own: InvariantsTest carries eight imports the split left dead (Body, CommitDelta, RunCommit, RunKey, ByteArrayInputStream, LinkedHashMap, Map, UUID) and InvariantsAcrossChainsTest imports FIXED_CLOCK without using it; and InvariantsAcrossChainsTest.java:329 closes with `.isEmpty();}}` on one line.

findings.title: The TRANSITIVE hop of the inheritance walk is unfalsified by this commit: deleting the recursion makes a real cross-epoch I2 reassignment SILENT, and only an untracked M4.20 file notices
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, one mutation applied alone to the staged bytes. Replace Invariants.java:247 `inherited.putAll(inheritedOffsets(store, prefix, prior, from, found, depth + 1));` with the same call discarding its result (`inheritedOffsets(store, prefix, prior, from, found, depth + 1);`) -- i.e. the ancestry walk still runs and still reports ancestor violations, but no ancestor's OFFSETS are inherited past one hop. Result: InvariantsTest and InvariantsAcrossChainsTest are ENTIRELY GREEN (17/17). The only test in the tree that dies is CommitProtocolSimulationTest#aCleanRunViolatesNothing -- and CommitProtocolSimulation, CommitProtocolSimulationTest and SimulatedClock are UNTRACKED files belonging to M4.20, so in a fresh clone at this commit the mutation leaves the suite green with nothing to notice. That is the same structural fact this row now leads with ('THIS ROW DELIVERS THE CLASS AS WELL AS ITS FIXTURES'): the class must stand on its own fixtures. THE MISS IS SILENT, not loud. Probed with a throwaway test against the staged bytes and then again under the mutation: epoch 1 = Continue(0,0,0), delta assigning 0..4, Seal(2, continuedAt=2); epoch 2 = Continue(0,1,2) then Seal(1, continuedAt=3) -- a leader that wrote its CONTINUE, committed nothing, and was sealed for its successor; epoch 3 = Continue(0,2,1), delta resuming at 0. Unmutated, checkChain(store, PREFIX, 3) returns [I2: stream RunKey[...aa, 0] resumes at 0 but the chain had assigned up to 5]. With line 247's result discarded it returns []. So a successor REASSIGNING five offsets that epoch 1 had already acknowledged is reported as clean -- verbatim the round-1 blocking defect ('the checker could not DISAGREE with production ... left it silent and the clean sweep green'), one hop further out. THE SHAPE IS THE COMMON ONE, not a contrivance: the never-opened while-loop at :226 handles a leader that died BEFORE writing its CONTINUE (Seal at slot 0); this recursion is the ONLY thing that handles a leader that wrote its CONTINUE and died before its first commit, which is the majority shape in the burned-epoch runs M4.16 records (73 epochs for 3 takeovers). Every cross-boundary fixture in the commit is one hop deep -- in each of them the recursive call returns an EMPTY map, so the transitive path is executed but never constrained. AND THE RISK IS IMMEDIATE: M4.24 is the row that rewrites this exact method for its O(E-squared) cost, and it would do so with a suite that cannot see the transitive hop disappear. SECONDARY, same walk and weaker, disclosed so it can be judged rather than found again: at Invariants.java:334 the `&& sealed.sequence() == 0` half of `neverOpened` is also unfalsified -- weakening it to `entries.getFirst() instanceof Seal` leaves the whole sequencer suite green (measured, 180 tests, exit 0). Its failure shape is a predecessor whose first surviving entry is a Seal at a NON-ZERO slot, which would then be stepped over as 'never opened' and its committed offsets dropped from the inheritance -- another silent miss, though only reachable when slot 0 is lost. Note that gutting the same method to `return false` IS killed, so it is specifically the sequence()==0 precision that is unconstrained. MINIMUM FIX, and it is not a split -- rule 12's remedy does not apply because this is one fixture, not a separable concern: add a two-hop fixture to InvariantsAcrossChainsTest built from the shape above (an OPENED, sealed, delta-free intermediate epoch) asserting I2 against the grandparent's high-water mark. If it is to be deferred instead, it needs a row that says so -- M4.22 is the observability accessor, M4.23 is the unsealed-ancestor blind spot plus the depth cap, M4.24 is the cost, and none of the three mentions the transitive inheritance hop, so as it stands a **done** row ships it unpinned and untracked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one fixture: epoch 1 commits and is sealed, epoch 2 writes only a CONTINUE and a SEAL, epoch 3 continues from 2 and rewinds -- assert I2 names epoch 1's high-water mark. Or defer it in an existing/new row.

findings.title: The row's last clause is a duplicated fragment that attributes the M4.23/M4.24 splits to the 500-line file split
findings.failure_scenario: The row states the round-2 split correctly -- 'At round 2 per rule 12: the observability accessor went to M4.22, the unsealed-ancestor blind spot and the depth cap to M4.23, the checker's own O(E-squared) cost to M4.24.' -- and then the sentence describing the SECOND split ('And again at 502 lines against the 500-line limit ... with `InvariantFixtures` holding the chain-building helpers both need so they cannot drift apart and still agree') ends by repeating twenty words of that clause verbatim: ', the unsealed-ancestor blind spot and the depth cap to M4.23, the checker's own O(E-squared) cost to M4.24'. As written the row says the 500-line file split moved those items, which is false -- the file split moved nothing between rows, it only divided one test class into two -- and the sentence terminates mid-clause with no full stop. CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE: this row exists in its current form because two earlier drafts described a commit other than themselves, and the M4.12 row above it carries three separate banners about the same mechanism. A reader reconstructing why M4.23 exists now gets two different answers from one row, and the milestone-review pass reads these rows as the record of what happened. Everything else checks out: the row names all four files (`Invariants`, `InvariantsTest`, `InvariantsAcrossChainsTest`, `InvariantFixtures`), both splits, and the deleted crossEpochOffsetsChecked(); its 'BOTH now pinned' claim about the two link arms is true by measurement; and its M4.23 correction reproduces. Per rule 11 this lands on a pass -- I am recording it, not asking for the round.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the duplicated trailing clause and end the sentence.
